bullets.text: Machine learning involves teaching computers to learn from data.
It's an alternative to explicit rule-based programming.
This lecture provides an overview of fundamental concepts.
Method where the system is trained using labeled data.
Examples include emails marked as spam or not spam.
The model learns patterns from this labeled input.
It then predicts outcomes for new, unseen cases.
Common algorithms: decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks.
System discovers patterns and structures in data without explicit labels.
Example: Grouping customers into clusters based on their purchasing behavior.
K-means is a classic algorithm used for clustering.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Learning occurs through feedback or rewards received from actions.
Famous applications include training AI to play video games.
Also used for controlling robots in complex environments.
Overfitting: Model memorizes training data too well, leading to poor performance on new data.
Bias: Occurs when the training data itself is not balanced or representative.
Addressing these challenges is crucial for robust models.
Healthcare: Used for disease prediction and diagnosis.
Finance: Essential for fraud detection and risk assessment.
Self-driving cars: Enables object recognition and navigation.
Machine learning is integrated into various industries.
The upcoming lecture will focus on how to evaluate machine learning models.
Key metrics to be covered include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.
Understanding these metrics is vital for assessing model performance.
